content: Eplerenone is a medication that can be used on its own or in combination with other drugs to manage high blood pressure. It belongs to a class of drugs known as mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists. This medication works by inhibiting the action of aldosterone, a naturally occurring hormone in the body that can increase blood pressure. Eplerenone is available in tablet form and is taken orally. It is typically taken once or twice daily, with or without food. To ensure consistent use, it is recommended to take the medication at the same time each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take eplerenone exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Your doctor may start you on a low dose and gradually increase it after four weeks. While eplerenone helps control high blood pressure, it does not cure the condition. It may take four weeks or longer to experience the full benefits of the medication. Continue taking eplerenone even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes. If you have questions about its use, ask your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before starting eplerenone, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to eplerenone or any other medications. Do not take eplerenone if you are using certain medications, such as amiloride, itraconazole, ketoconazole, potassium supplements, spironolactone, triamterene, or specific combinations of these drugs. Provide your doctor and pharmacist with a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking, as some may interact with eplerenone. This includes drugs like erythromycin, fluconazole, fluoxetine, HIV protease inhibitors, lithium, metronidazole, verapamil, and others. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Additionally, inform your doctor if you are taking herbal products, especially St. John’s wort. Let your doctor know if you have or have ever had high potassium levels, diabetes, gout, or liver or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking eplerenone, contact your doctor immediately. Discuss with your doctor whether you can consume grapefruit juice while taking this medication. Avoid using salt substitutes containing potassium. If your doctor prescribes a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose of eplerenone, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Eplerenone may cause side effects. Common side effects include headache, dizziness, diarrhea, stomach pain, cough, fatigue, flu-like symptoms, breast enlargement or tenderness, and abnormal vaginal bleeding. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience chest pain, tingling in your arms or legs, loss of muscle tone, weakness or heaviness in your legs, confusion, lack of energy, cold or gray skin, or an irregular heartbeat. If you notice any unusual problems while taking this medication, inform your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store eplerenone in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include fainting, dizziness, blurred vision, upset stomach, tingling in the arms and legs, loss of muscle tone, weakness or heaviness in the legs, confusion, lack of energy, cold or gray skin, and irregular or slow heartbeat. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will monitor your blood pressure and may order lab tests to assess your response to eplerenone. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
